correctness.rationale: Exact square-line clipping and induced-plane Jacobian yield the all-normal arctangent area formula. For fixed vertical normal coordinate, strict convexity of an explicit integral representation of \(h_c^\prime\) proves the horizontal-diagonal unique maximum. The inequality \(\arctan x>3x/(x^2+3)\) proves the diagonal profile has precisely one minimum and endpoint global maximum \(\pi\sqrt2\). Euclidean ball containment and positive-angle strictness prove the minimum \(\pi\) and its exact equality normals. Independent finite polar quadrature passed 154 instances, not used as a proof.

value.rationale: The maximum central planar section of the classical bicylinder is a motivated natural extremal invariant. The claim supplies a complete direction-dependent area formula and sharp classification of both min and max planes; it is not a routine single-section computation. A strict convexity-of-centered-means lemma collapses a nontrivial two-parameter orientation optimization and reveals a nonmonotone diagonal profile, giving a reproducible exact benchmark for intersection-body geometry.
